text:
+ Name: Emilio Varela Montes
+ CA: 2;2; 26 months
+ Context: Bilingual home visit and initial IFSP planning; English and Spanish during play, snack, and family conversation.
+ Date: October 8, 2026
+ Clinician: Marina Reyes, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist, Little Lantern Pediatric Communication Services
+ Record: IFSP-72640519; NC ITP child ID: NCITP-60829471

Summary / Resumen

Emilio participated in this fictional NC Infant-Toddler Program planning visit with his parents, Lucía Montes and Daniel Varela. The family requested support for communication during ordinary activities, especially meals, getting dressed, and transitions between caregivers. Spanish is the main language at home. English occurs during childcare and some community activities. The family wants both languages included without pressure to replace Spanish. The team identified strengths in shared enjoyment, imitation of familiar actions, and interest in songs. Communication becomes harder when adults ask several questions together or move quickly between activities. This IFSP addresses participation and caregiver support through play and daily routines. All people, organizations, identifiers, and events in this document are fictional.

Información de la familia

The family lives at 418 Meadow Lantern Lane, apartment 2B, Larkmeadow, North Carolina 27843, in Willowbend County. Their mailing address is the same. The preferred contact is mamá Lucía, at 919-555-0146 or lucia.montes@example.com. Papá Daniel can receive scheduling calls at 984-555-0182. The parents prefer Spanish for explanations about consent and English for brief appointment reminders. They requested telephone contact before an unfamiliar provider visits. The family understands that a bilingual visit can include either language, según la rutina, and that a caregiver may ask for clarification at any point.

The household includes sister Sol Varela Montes, who is 6 years old, and brother Nico Varela Montes, who is 4 years old. Their grandmother, Teresa Montes, provides afternoon care. An aunt, Elena Varela, helps with transportation when the parents’ schedules overlap. The family’s dog, Pipo, usually rests behind a gate during visits. Sister Sol attends Lantern Grove Elementary School. Brother Nico attends Little Acorn Bilingual Childcare. The parents describe the siblings as patient play partners, but they want adults to carry responsibility for communication practice.

Work schedules / Horarios de trabajo

Mamá Lucía works morning shifts at the store Blue Lantern Market, which she calls Mercado del Farol Azul in Spanish. She also accepts occasional shifts at the restaurant Copper Spoon Kitchen, or Restaurante de la Cuchara de Cobre, and cleans offices through the cleaning service Clear Nest Cleaning Service, or Servicio de Limpieza Nido Claro. She said, “Mis horarios cambian. Necesito ideas que caben mientras preparo comida, no otra tarea larga.” The team will place practice within existing activities and avoid assigning a separate daily lesson that competes with meals or rest.

Papá Daniel currently works at the factory Cedar Thread Manufacturing Plant, described in Spanish as Planta de Manufactura Hilo de Cedro. His seasonal work includes the farm Morning Finch Farm, or Granja del Pinzón de la Mañana, and the construction company Stone Lantern Construction Company, or Compañía de Construcción Farol de Piedra. He said, “Cuando llego, quiero jugar con él. Show me something simple que puedo hacer con los zapatos o la pelota.” Evening demonstrations will use familiar objects and short routines. The family will report schedule changes directly to the coordinator.

Coordinación y otras agencias

Service coordinator Ana Beltrán works through Willowbend Children’s Developmental Services Agency, the family’s CDSA office, at 72 Juniper Window Drive, Larkmeadow, North Carolina 27843. Her telephone is 919-555-0127, and her email is ana.beltran@example.com. She will coordinate referrals, explain service options in Spanish, and check whether proposed visit times fit the caregivers’ schedules. The family requested one calendar showing all agreed visits. Coordinator A. Beltrán will also confirm who should receive copies of the plan before distributing them.

The family receives nutrition support through Willowbend Family Nutrition Office and transportation information from Willowbend Community Assistance Department. They also participate in Red Comunitaria de Acompañamiento Familiar y Desarrollo Temprano del Condado de Willowbend (RCAFDT). Later coordination with RCAFDT will focus on Spanish family activities and available transportation. Childcare teacher Ms. Rosa Pineda agreed to share observations after the parents sign the appropriate release. Community driver J. Ortiz is listed only as a transportation contact. He will not receive clinical reports or participate in treatment decisions.

Health and administrative information

The child’s date of birth is August 8, 2024. The family reported birth at Juniper Harbor Community Hospital, gestational age 39 weeks, birth weight 3.24 kg, and Apgar scores 8 and 9. Pediatrician Dr. Clara Soria follows routine care through Meadow Lantern Pediatric Center. The parents reported no current hearing concern. A hearing screening referral remains part of the plan because the team wants current information before interpreting changes in spoken communication. The coordinator will help the family schedule it and obtain the report.

The Medicaid ID is 482716905Q. The insurance member ID is MLH-730482196, through Meadow Lantern Health Plan. The service authorization number is AUTH-SLP-261008-43. Proposed speech-language documentation uses CPT 92507 with modifier GN and ICD-10 F80.2. These administrative entries belong to this fictional record. Coordinator Ana Beltrán will verify authorization details before services begin. The family requested that full identifiers appear only on necessary forms and that appointment reminders use the child’s first name.

Preocupaciones y prioridades: palabras de la familia

Mamá Lucía said, “Él sabe lo que quiere, pero sometimes I cannot understand. Se enoja cuando adivino mal.” Papá Daniel added, “Quiero que pueda pedir ayuda sin llorar tanto. No necesito palabras perfectas; quiero entenderlo.” Grandmother Teresa said, “Cuando vamos despacio, él participa más. Necesito aprender cómo esperar.” The parents prioritize requesting help, choosing food or toys, and joining sibling play. They also want a shared response when the child points, signs, or uses a word approximation. Speech clarity is a secondary concern within these participation goals.

The family does not want adults to require repeated imitation before giving a needed item. Mamá Lucía explained, “Si tiene hambre, primero lo escuchamos. Practice can happen mientras comemos.” The team agreed to acknowledge any clear communication attempt, offer a brief model, and continue the activity. Papá Daniel prefers demonstrations followed by his own practice. Grandmother Teresa prefers a short Spanish note with one example. The clinician will adapt each visit to these preferences and ask caregivers which strategy felt useful between visits.

Rutinas diarias

Breakfast usually begins at 7:15 a.m.. The child sits beside grandmother Teresa and reaches toward preferred foods. Adults often anticipate his request before he communicates. The family will try showing two available choices, naming each once, and waiting. At dressing time, around 8:00 a.m., the child helps push his arms through sleeves but protests when a shoe feels tight. The caregiver can pause, show the shoe, and model "ayuda" or "help". The aim is a useful exchange that lets dressing continue with less frustration.

Childcare occurs at Little Acorn Bilingual Childcare on the parents’ scheduled workdays. Teacher Ms. Pineda reported that Emi watches peers before joining. Classmate Maya Quintero often offers blocks, while friend Leo Duarte enjoys rolling cars beside him. Group member Inés Calder sometimes chooses the same toy. Staff will offer short models during these exchanges and help children take turns without requiring spoken words. The family wants childcare observations to include the situation, the child’s attempt, and the adult’s response, rather than a list of missed words.

Lunch begins near 12:10 p.m., followed by quiet play and rest. The family notices more gestures when the room is calm. Afternoon play at 4:30 p.m. often includes a ball, toy animals, or pictures with siblings. Dinner is usually at 6:20 p.m., though work shifts can change it. Bath and bedtime routines begin near 7:40 p.m.. The parents prefer songs and familiar books at bedtime. They requested that communication practice remain brief when the child is tired and that adults stop if the activity becomes a struggle.

Communication observations / Observaciones

During the assessment on September 29, 2026, the clinician used PLS-5 tasks alongside bilingual observation, caregiver interview, and play samples. The fictional score sheet lists Auditory Comprehension standard score 78, percentile 7, confidence interval 73-85, and age equivalent 1;8. It lists Expressive Communication standard score 75, percentile 5, confidence interval 70-83, and age equivalent 1;5. The Total Language standard score is 74, percentile 4, with confidence interval 69-82. These entries do not capture all skills across both languages.

In play, Emilio followed familiar directions in 7/10 opportunities with gestures and min cues. He selected a named familiar object in 3 of 5 opportunities. He used a gesture, sound, or word approximation in 60% of observed requesting opportunities with mod cues. Productions included "agua", "más", "go", and "ba". A sample recorded "agua agua" [EW when he repeated a request. He also said "Pipo ven" and "Sol mira". Those named productions were recorded separately from ordinary vocabulary targets.

Speech observations included emerging / consonant patterns such as /m/, /b/, and /p/, with occasional [w] in word approximations. The clinician will observe /k/ and Spanish /ɾ/ within meaningful words as vocabulary expands. No isolated sound drill is included in this initial plan. The family chose the target word "sol" for a picture of the sun. Sister Sol has the same spelling as that target. Adults will use context to distinguish the vocabulary word "sol" from the sibling’s name, Sol.

Resultados y estrategias

Outcome 1: During meals and play, Emilio will communicate a choice or request through a gesture, sign, picture, sound, or word in 8/10 natural opportunities across two caregivers. The family will record brief examples during ordinary routines. The clinician will model Enhanced Milieu Teaching strategies, including accessible choices, responsive language models, and pauses. Caregivers will begin with mod cues and reduce support toward min cues when the child initiates more often. Target words include "más", "agua", "pan", "more", and "open", selected according to the routine and language used.

For Outcome 1, breakfast practice can begin with two foods already available. The caregiver will hold them where the child can see them, name them, and wait. If he points, the caregiver will acknowledge the choice and provide it. A short expansion can follow, such as "más pan". The clinician will ask the caregiver to explain what happened and choose one adjustment. The family may try Hanen responsive interaction strategies during shared play. The team will use caregiver examples to judge whether the approach fits the family’s day.

Outcome 2: During dressing, toy play, and transitions, Emilio will request help or indicate a problem in 4 of 5 opportunities with min cues. Adults will accept a gesture, a help sign, or words such as "ayuda", "help", and "no". The clinician will demonstrate Functional Communication Training within safe, naturally occurring difficulties, such as a closed container or a tangled sleeve. Adults will respond promptly. They will not create distress to obtain a response. Progress will include clearer communication and smoother participation, even when the child’s spoken form remains approximate.

For Outcome 2, the parents will choose one predictable situation each week. Papá Daniel selected shoes because he usually helps with them after work. Mamá Lucía selected opening the snack container. Grandmother Teresa selected asking for assistance with a toy lid. The same simple response will follow each attempt: acknowledge, help, and model. If the child becomes upset, the adult will provide support and return to communication later. The coordinator will check whether the selected situations remain practical when work schedules change.

Outcome 3: During sibling or childcare play, Emilio will join a shared activity for at least four reciprocal turns in 3 of 4 observed routines with mod cues or less. Strategies include Naturalistic Developmental Behavioral Intervention techniques within preferred play, simple turn signals, and short language models. Teacher Ms. Rosa Pineda will offer a rolling car or block exchange with peer Maya. At home, sister Sol may offer a ball when she wants to participate. Adults will guide the exchange and let siblings return to their own activities.

Service plan / Fechas de servicio

Speech-language services will begin on October 15, 2026 and continue through April 14, 2027, with one weekly home or childcare visit lasting forty-five minutes. Clinician Marina Reyes will provide bilingual services through Little Lantern Pediatric Communication Services. The usual appointment is Thursday at 4:15 p.m.. Coordinator Ana Beltrán will provide monthly coordination from October 8, 2026 through April 14, 2027. The team scheduled the review for January 14, 2027. Interpreter Estela Ríos is available if another provider cannot conduct a needed discussion in Spanish.

Seguimiento y acuerdo familiar

Caregivers will share two brief examples per week: what the child wanted, how he communicated, and what helped. The clinician will document cueing levels and progress toward Outcomes 1, 2, and 3. At the review, the team will compare participation across routines and revise strategies with the family. Mamá Lucía said, “Este plan sí cabe en nuestra vida.” Papá Daniel agreed to practice during shoes and ball play. The coordinator will provide the completed plan in the family’s preferred format and confirm the first visit by telephone.

The coordinator will arrange visits around the parents’ work schedules. Mom works nights at Moonbrook Packaging Works as a packaging line inspector. Dad works as a maintenance assistant at Harbor Reed Apartments. Their schedules change monthly. Text reminders are preferred, followed by telephone calls when a decision needs discussion. The mother checks email on days off.

Preocupaciones y prioridades / Family voice

Mother: “Quiero que Marijo nos diga lo que necesita sin llorar tanto. Sometimes I know she wants something, pero no sé cuál. I want her to say ‘ayuda’ or show me before she gets upset.”

Father: “En la cena estamos todos juntos. I want her to ask for ‘más’ and tell us when she is finished. No queremos quitarle el español. Her grandparents need to understand her, too.”

The parents identified three priorities: easier requests during meals, shared play with her brother, and smoother daycare transitions. They prefer strategies that fit existing activities. They do not want worksheets or repeated demands to imitate. The clinician explained that gestures, pointing, pictures, and spoken words can work together. La familia agreed that successful communication matters more than using one particular form.

Historia y salud / Relevant background

The child was born at 35 weeks, 4 days gestation, with birth weight 2,310 g. Reported Apgar scores were 7 and 9. She received feeding observation at Willow Meridian Health Briar Cove Campus NICU and went home on August 21, 2024.

Primary care physician Dr. Camila Soler sees her at Willow Meridian Health Briar Cove Campus Pediatric Clinic. An appointment at Willow Meridian Health Briar Cove Campus ENT and Audiology occurred on September 23, 2026. Audiologist Owen Lira documented responses adequate for the communication activities sampled. The family will follow the practice’s recommendation for monitoring after another ear infection.

The mother reported no current feeding restrictions, prescribed hearing devices, or medication changes. These reports were reviewed for planning; the IFSP team did not conduct a medical examination. The coordinator will request updated records with the family’s authorization.

Evaluación y observaciones / Communication profile

Resultado 1 / Requests during meals

+ Name: Nicolás de la Cruz-Morales
+ CA: 2;4; 28 months
+ Context: Bilingual home visit; fictional North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program IFSP review
+ Date: 3 de marzo de 2025

Summary

This fictional review describes Nicolás’s communication across home, childcare, and community routines. Spanish is the main home language; English occurs during childcare and errands. The family reports more gestures and shared play since the initial IFSP. Spoken messages remain short and inconsistent. The team recommends continued coaching within familiar activities, with attention to requesting, understanding directions, and repairing communication breakdowns. All personal details, organizations, contacts, and record numbers in this document are invented for testing.

Información de la familia

Nicolás de la Cruz-Morales lives with his mother, Lucía de la Cruz, his father, Andrés Morales, and his sister, Elena Morales, age 6;1. The home address is 1847 Willow Lantern Drive, Cedar Hollow, North Carolina 27900, in Bellflower County. His maternal grandmother, Rosa del Río, provides care during overlapping work shifts. His aunt, Beatriz de la Cruz, sometimes helps with transportation. The family’s dog, Chispa, joins outdoor play and often motivates requests.

Lucía works two jobs: a morning shift at LMP and evening cleaning at Willow Lantern Suites. The first workplace is recorded only by its acronym, as requested by the family. Andrés works at Cedar Hollow Cabinet Works. The parents prefer visits before the evening shift. They identify their hometown village as San Jacinto de las Nubes, Mexico. A family mailing address there is Calle del Colibrí 27, Barrio Las Brisas, San Jacinto de las Nubes. No international correspondence is planned.

The preferred telephone number is 919-555-0146. A backup number for Andrés is 984-555-0173. The family’s fictional email is lucia.delacruz@example.invalid. The child’s fictional Medicaid identifier is 583027461Q. The service authorization is AUTH-FICT-250310-SL. Family contact information must be checked privately before scheduling. Spanish messages are preferred; either parent can read brief English reminders.

Coordinación de servicios

The service coordinator is Camila Torres, at Bellflower Children’s Developmental Services Agency. The office address is 620 Meadow Lantern Road, Cedar Hollow, North Carolina 27900. Contact: 252-555-0128, camila.torres@example.invalid. The fictional family information page is https://bellflower-cdsa.example.invalid/familias. Camila Torres will coordinate referrals, interpreter requests, and scheduling. The family prefers direct Spanish communication, with an interpreter available when another team member needs language support.

Preocupaciones y prioridades: en sus propias palabras

Lucía stated, “Quiero entender lo que necesita sin estar adivinando. Cuando estoy entre mis dos trabajos, necesito que la abuela use las mismas ideas. No quiero otra lista larga de homework.” She identified meals and departures as the hardest routines. She wants communication support that fits the family’s schedule. Her first priority is helping Nicolás ask for food, help, and another turn before frustration becomes intense.

Andrés stated, “En español entiende nuestras cosas, pero afuera todo va rápido en English. Quiero que pueda decir que necesita ayuda.” He wants childcare staff to accept Spanish words, gestures, and pictures. Rosa del Río added, “Si me enseña o me señala, yo le respondo. Quiero saber cuándo esperar y cuándo ayudar.” The family values connection and participation over clear pronunciation during every interaction.

The parents also want Elena to enjoy play without becoming responsible for therapy. Lucía said, “Que sea su hermana, no su maestra.” The team agreed that adults will carry the strategies. The family declined extra worksheets and requested brief demonstrations, practice during real routines, and a short Spanish summary after each visit.

Rutinas diarias

Breakfast starts near 6:45 a.m.. Rosa offers familiar foods while Lucía prepares for work. Nicolás reaches toward containers, points, and sometimes says “más”. When an adult guesses too quickly, he has little reason to send another message. The family will offer a visible choice, pause briefly, and respond to any clear communication. Food will remain available; adults will not require a spoken word before meeting a need.

Childcare arrival occurs around 8:10 a.m. at Little Lantern Early Learning House. Ms. Iris Salgado supports the transition; assistant Devon Price helps during snack and outdoor play. Familiar peers include Maya Chen and Tomás Rivera. Nicolás watches their play, brings objects close, and sometimes leaves when several children talk together. A quiet greeting, a predictable picture sequence, and one available play partner help him participate.

After pickup at 4:35 p.m., the family usually plays outside or prepares dinner. Bath and bedtime begin near 7:20 p.m.. Nicolás enjoys pouring water, animal books, and chasing bubbles with Chispa. During the visit, he said “Chispa ven” and later “Elena mira.” These messages were acknowledged immediately. Adults will use bath toys and shared books for natural language practice, while keeping bedtime calm and flexible.

Historia del desarrollo y salud

The fictional birth date is 11/03/2022. Delivery occurred at Meadow Lantern Community Hospital, at 37 weeks, 2 days gestation. Birth weight was 6 pounds, 8 ounces. Recorded Apgar scores were 8 and 9. The family reports no current feeding restriction or prescribed communication device. Pediatrician Dr. Esteban Ríos at Cedar Hollow Children’s Clinic follows development. Hearing screening documentation dated 2025-02-12 reports results within the screening criteria; this review does not substitute for a diagnostic hearing evaluation.

Evaluación bilingüe

During the evaluation on 02/18/2025, the clinician used caregiver interview, observation, language sampling, and selected PLS-5 Spanish activities. Auditory Comprehension and Expressive Communication tasks helped describe skills. The clinician did not report standard scores, percentiles, confidence intervals, or age equivalents because the administration included adaptations. English childcare information and Spanish home observations were considered together. Difficulty across both settings supports continued intervention; exposure to two languages alone does not explain the concerns.

In a familiar play sample, Nicolás followed related directions in 7/10 opportunities with min cues. He communicated requests through speech, gesture, or pictures in 6 of 8 opportunities. Independent spoken messages occurred in 40% of observed opportunities. Productions included “agua”, “más pan”, and “go”. The clinician documented [EW] when an extra word occurred. Speech observations included variable /k/, emerging /m/, and occasional [w]; Spanish /ɾ/ was not a current treatment priority.

Otras agencias y apoyos

Bellflower Family Nutrition Office provides nutrition support, and Cedar Hollow Family Resource Partnership offers a Spanish caregiver group. Bellflower Family Services Department previously helped the family locate transportation information. The family remembers an intake conversation on el martes 4 de junio de 2024. No active child protection involvement is reported. These supports are separate from speech services. The coordinator will confirm which contacts the parents want included in future planning.

Meadow Lantern Primary School serves Elena. School communication does not authorize sharing this IFSP. Occupational therapist Nora Whitfield is available through the CDSA for consultation if sensory or participation concerns persist. Interpreter Pilar Acosta can support meetings when needed. The family wants referrals explained in Spanish before contact occurs. Camila Torres will document consent and avoid duplicate appointments during the parents’ work shifts.

Resultados y estrategias

Outcome 1: During meals and snacks, Nicolás will request an item, another portion, or help using a word, gesture, or picture in 8/10 opportunities across home and childcare routines. Adults will place choices where he can see them, model “más”, “agua”, and “help”, then wait. A clear gesture counts as success. The family will practice during one chosen meal rather than every meal. Progress will be reviewed through caregiver examples and brief observation. The current baseline is 6/10 with mod cues; the target is participation with min cues.

Outcome 2: During dressing and departures, Nicolás will follow a familiar direction and complete the next routine step in 4 of 5 opportunities. Adults will pair simple language with a gesture or picture, using Spanish at home and familiar English at childcare. Models include “zapatos aquí” and “coat on”. The adult will reduce competing talk and allow time for a response. The family will choose the language that fits the interaction. Baseline performance is 2 of 5 with max cues. Success will include participation across different caregivers, with min cues.

Outcome 3: During play, Nicolás will share attention and exchange turns with an adult or peer for 3 of 4 observed play sequences. Adults will follow his interest, imitate actions, and add a short model such as “mi turno” or “your turn”. Ms. Salgado will support play with Maya or Tomás when the group is calm. No peer will be assigned responsibility for teaching. The baseline is 1 of 4 sequences with mod cues. Caregiver notes will describe enjoyment, persistence, and the help needed.

Outcome 4: When a message is misunderstood, Nicolás will try another communication method in 3 of 5 naturally occurring opportunities. Adults will acknowledge the first attempt and offer a simple repair option: show, point, bring a picture, or try another word. Models include “ayuda” and “show me”. The family will stop practice if distress increases. Baseline performance is 1 of 5 with max cues. The target is repair with min cues, while adults remain responsible for noticing and responding to his needs.

Outcome 5: The parents and grandmother will identify and use two communication strategies during their selected routines in 4 of 5 observed opportunities. Strategies include following the child’s lead, pausing, offering choices, and expanding a message. Lucía will choose breakfast; Andrés will choose bath; Rosa will choose afternoon play. The clinician will demonstrate, invite practice, and ask what felt useful. The baseline is 2 of 5 opportunities. The family may change routines when work demands change. A missed practice day does not count as caregiver failure.

Enfoques clínicos

Coaching will draw from Hanen and It Takes Two to Talk, with strategies explained in Spanish and English. Picture exchange principles from PECS may support functional requests when appropriate. PROMPT, Cycles, and Kaufman were discussed as named approaches, not prescribed as a combined package. The current plan emphasizes communication and participation. Structured speech work will follow further assessment of speech patterns and motor needs. The clinician will explain the reason for any approach before using it and will check that the family can apply the chosen strategies comfortably.

Fechas y servicios

The initial IFSP date was 12/09/2024. This review occurred on 03/03/2025. Speech-language services will continue from 2025-03-10 through 09/09/2025, once weekly for forty-five minutes in home or childcare routines. The next planned visit is 3/10/25 at 9:15 a.m.. Service coordination continues throughout that period. The billing references are CPT 92507, modifier GN, and ICD-10 F80.2. Authorization and actual attendance must be verified separately. These dates describe the fictional plan, not completed visits.

Seguimiento y acuerdo familiar

The next review is planned for 9 de junio de 2025. Marisol Vega-Santillán will summarize progress using observed routines and family reports. Camila Torres will check scheduling and referral needs. The parents received a Spanish explanation and requested a bilingual copy. Lucía stated, “Así sí cabe en nuestro día.” Andrés agreed with the priorities. Audiology documentation dated September 22, 2026 recorded hearing responses adequate for the assessment conditions. Parents will report new concerns about hearing, ear discomfort, or changes in responses to voices. No swallowing assessment occurred during this review.

ASSESSMENT SNAPSHOT / RESUMEN DE EVALUACIÓN

PLS-5: Auditory Comprehension	Standard score 78	7th percentile	90% interval 73-83	1;9–2;2

The English standardized scores are recorded for continuity. Spanish responses and supported bilingual probes informed intervention planning but were not substituted into standardized scoring. The descriptive play range is not a norm-referenced result. Age equivalents do not define the child’s developmental age or determine eligibility by themselves.

During play, Elian produced “más agua,” “open,” and “no mío.” He said “Chispa ven” while approaching the gate. This last production contains the pet’s name and is documented as spoken.

Observed speech included [w] for some rounded-word beginnings and variable production of /k/. The Spanish tap /ɾ/ was not targeted. The clinician used min cues for familiar requests and mod cues when introducing new combinations. One sample contained an extra word, coded [EW] during transcript review.

DAILY ROUTINES / RUTINAS DEL DÍA

During snack observation, the child selected a cup through pointing and then added “agua.” Mother expanded this to “más agua” without requiring repetition. The child remained engaged and independently used the longer phrase later.

At daycare, classmates Lina Osel and Tavo Merel enjoy the same rolling-ball activity. The teacher reports that parallel play often becomes shared play when an adult provides a clear turn sequence. Staff will offer communication opportunities during activities the child already chooses.

The babysitter will use the same picture choices at home. Grandmother prefers spoken models paired with gestures. Both options remain available because the family values flexibility across caregivers.

Volunteer Celia Braven leads the library’s family song circle. Participation is optional and is not a therapy requirement. The coordinator will share only information authorized by the parents. The family requests that therapy notes stay within the agreed service team.

OUTCOME 1 / PEDIR AYUDA EN LAS RUTINAS

By January 8, 2027, the child will request an item, help, or continuation using a word, word combination, gesture, or picture in 8/10 natural opportunities across meals and play, with min cues, as documented by caregiver report and session observation.

Baseline: independent communication occurred in 4/10 observed opportunities. Requests increased to 7/10 with mod cues. Adults will honor clear gestures while modeling language. They will place desired materials within view, offer an achievable choice, and pause before helping.

Strategies use Hanen principles, responsive interaction, and short bilingual models. Suggested targets include “ayuda,” “abre,” and “more bubbles.” The target word “sol” means the sun in a picture book. The sister’s name is Sol. Adults will keep these meanings clear through context.

OUTCOME 2 / ENTENDER Y PARTICIPAR

By January 8, 2027, the child will follow a familiar direction during dressing, cleanup, or snack in 3 of 5 opportunities across two routines, with min cues. Directions may be given in Spanish or English according to the routine.

Baseline was 2 of 5 with mod cues. Adults will gain attention, provide one short direction, and pair it with a natural gesture. Examples include “pon aquí” and “get shoes.” They will allow processing time before repeating.

The clinician will coach caregivers to reduce competing speech and expand successful routines gradually. Performance will be reviewed separately by language and context when enough observations are available. A missed direction during distress will prompt support and observation, rather than repeated testing.

OUTCOME 3 / JUGAR CON OTROS

By January 8, 2027, the child will participate in a shared play sequence with a peer or sibling for three reciprocal turns in 80% of observed opportunities, with mod cues or less.

Baseline shared participation was 40%. Adults will model “mi turno,” “your turn,” and “otra vez.” They will accept passing an object, looking toward a partner, or using a picture as participation. Spoken words are welcome but are not required for each turn.

Visits are planned for Fridays at 10:30 a.m.. Parents may request another time when work shifts change. Codes document the planned services; they do not guarantee payment. The coordinator will verify authorization before the first scheduled intervention visit.

REVIEW, AGREEMENT, AND NEXT STEPS / ACUERDOS

The team will review progress on January 8, 2027. Caregivers will share brief examples from routines rather than complete daily worksheets. The clinician will document communication opportunities, support levels, and whether skills transfer between people and settings.

The team discussed transition planning before the child’s third birthday on April 12, 2027. The coordinator will explain available options and obtain required consent before sharing records. The family requested Spanish explanations during that discussion.

Parents agreed with the outcomes and proposed schedule. Mother summarized, “Pequeños pasos, todos los días, sin quitarle sus dos idiomas.” Father requested coaching during dinner when scheduling permits. The clinician will begin with snack and play, then extend strategies to dinner.

NC INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM IFSP REVIEW — REVISIÓN BILINGÜE

- This fictional review documents family priorities, participation, progress, and planned early intervention supports. English and Spanish were used according to each participant’s preference. The family reviewed the plan aloud and received both language versions.
- Review date: October 7, 2026. Initial IFSP date: April 8, 2026. Next review: April 7, 2027. Child record: NCIT-682041. Medicaid member number: 581027643K.

FAMILY INFORMATION — INFORMACIÓN FAMILIAR

- Emilio Cárdenas Solís, called Milo at home, was born August 12, 2024 and is 25 months old. The family lives at 418 Lantern Plum Lane, Alder Finch, North Carolina 27863, in Larkhaven County.
- His mother, Mariela Solís, and father, Tomás Cárdenas, share decision-making. His sister, Inés Cárdenas Solís, is 6 years old. His grandmother, Rosa Solís, provides afternoon care.
- Preferred contact: 919-555-0146 or mariela.solis@example.org. His father works at Copper Finch Packaging. The household speaks mostly Spanish, with English during books and community activities.

SERVICE COORDINATION — COORDINACIÓN

- Service coordinator Lidia Navarro works through Lantern Valley CDSA, located at 72 Willow Compass Court, Alder Finch, North Carolina 27863. Office telephone: 919-555-0172. Family information page: https://lanterncdsa.example.org/familias.
- Bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist Camila Varela provides services through Small Lantern Pediatric Communication. Scheduling contact: 919-555-0184. The family prefers Spanish explanations followed by brief English written summaries.
- Interpreter J. Aranda remains available for meetings with English-speaking providers. The coordinator will arrange transportation support when needed and confirm changes by telephone. The family requested one shared calendar to reduce missed appointments.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY — HISTORIA MÉDICA

- Emilio was born at Juniper Bell Children’s Hospital at 35 weeks, 4 days gestation, with birth weight 2,260 g. Apgar scores were 7 and 9. The NICU stay lasted eleven days for feeding support and temperature monitoring.
- Neonatologist Dr. Anika Serrano documented stable discharge. Pediatrician Dr. Owen Mireles follows growth and development. Otolaryngologist Dr. Nadia Ferral evaluated recurrent ear infections on June 18, 2026.
- Audiologist Brielle Duarte reported hearing adequate for speech access on July 9, 2026. No current swallowing concerns were reported. Parents describe picky eating, especially mixed textures, without coughing or choking during meals.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES — NUESTRAS PALABRAS

- His mother said, “Quiero que Milo me diga lo que necesita. When he pulls my hand, sometimes I understand, pero otras veces termina llorando. I want him to have a way to ask before he gets frustrated.”
- His father said, “En la casa habla más. Around other people, se queda calladito. We want both languages supported because that is how our family talks.”
- His grandmother said, “Que participe en la mesa, aunque sea poquito. I want meals to feel calm.” The family prioritized requesting help, joining play, and using familiar words during meals.

STRENGTHS AND DAILY ROUTINES — LO QUE YA FUNCIONA

- Morning begins near 6:45 a.m.. Dressing works best when an adult offers two visible choices. Emilio smiles during predictable songs and copies gestures before attempting words. The family can practice briefly while finding shoes.
- Breakfast occurs around 7:20 a.m.. He points toward preferred food and sometimes says “más”. Adults usually respond quickly; they agreed to pause briefly and acknowledge gestures, sounds, or words without requiring repetition.
- Evening play includes blocks, picture books, and the family dog, Nube. During observation, he said “Nube ven.” His sister enjoys taking turns with animal figures. Bedtime starts near 8:00 p.m. with songs and quiet books.

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION — APOYOS Y OTRAS AGENCIAS

- Emilio attends The Velvet Acorn Observatory on weekday mornings. Teacher Ms. Pilar Fenwick and classroom assistant M.R. report that he watches classmates before joining. Peers Lena Quill and Dario Bellín often offer him blocks.
- The family receives nutrition support through Larkhaven County WIC. Contact Alma Reedwell coordinates appointments. Larkhaven County Partnership for Children supplied bilingual books and information about playgroups.
- Larkhaven County Early Head Start has an intake scheduled for October 22, 2026. With written family consent, the coordinator will share functional communication priorities and request information about classroom routines.

ASSESSMENT AND CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS — EVALUACIÓN

- Evaluation on September 23, 2026 included the PLS-5 Spanish, caregiver interview, and play observation across languages. Auditory Comprehension standard score: 78; percentile: 7; confidence interval: 73-85.
- Expressive Communication standard score: 74; percentile: 4; confidence interval: 69-82. Reported age-equivalent range: 1;6–1;10. Scores were interpreted alongside language exposure and everyday participation.
- Clinical diagnosis: F80.2. He followed familiar directions in 8/10 opportunities, or 80%, with min cues. Spontaneous requests occurred in 3 of 5 opportunities during preferred play.

COMMUNICATION SAMPLE — MUESTRA DE LENGUAJE

- Productions included “agua”, “más pan”, “open”, and “help me”. The clinician accepted either language and modeled slightly longer messages without asking the family to replace Spanish with English.
- Speech included [ [KEEP|w] ] for an emerging sound; phonetic transcription: [w]. Attempts at /k/ and /ɾ/ were inconsistent. Speech sound accuracy will be monitored within meaningful words.
- The sample contained one word-level error coded [EW]. This code describes the sample only. The team emphasized communicative success, shared attention, and participation during familiar routines.

OUTCOME 1 — PEDIR AYUDA Y HACER ELECCIONES

- During meals and dressing, Emilio will request an item or help using a gesture, picture, sound, or word in 4 of 5 opportunities across three consecutive family logs.
- Strategies include focused stimulation, visible choices, and models such as “ayuda”, “help”, and “más agua”. Adults will respond to the message immediately. The clinician will demonstrate and coach practice within the existing routine.

OUTCOME 2 — PARTICIPAR CON OTROS

- During classroom or sibling play, Milo will initiate or respond during a shared activity in 3 of 5 opportunities, with mod cues or less, across three observations.
- Adults will use naturalistic language intervention and Hanen strategies: follow his interest, pause, and model a short turn. Teacher Ms. Fenwick will record one example weekly. No verbal response is required to receive a toy.

OUTCOME 3 — ENTENDER RUTINAS

- During cleanup and bedtime, Emilio will follow familiar one-step directions with 80% accuracy and min cues across three routine samples.
- The family will pair gestures with consistent words, then reduce support gradually. Models include “pon aquí” and “give me”. The clinician will check understanding in both languages and adjust vocabulary to family use.

SERVICES, DATES, AND RESPONSIBILITIES — SERVICIOS

- Speech-language intervention: weekly, forty-five minutes, from October 14, 2026 through April 7, 2027, at home or the classroom. Provider: Camila Varela. Billing reference: CPT 92507, modifier GN, diagnosis F80.2.
- Evaluation completed September 23, 2026: CPT 92523, modifier GN. Authorization: AUTH-6401829. Occupational therapist Elena Briseno will consult on mealtime participation beginning October 28, 2026.
- The coordinator will contact the family monthly. Parents will choose feasible practice moments; classroom staff will share brief observations. Strategies will change when routines become stressful or the child’s participation decreases.

REVIEW AGREEMENT — ACUERDOS

- The family agreed that bilingual communication, gestures, and pictures all count toward functional progress. No home language change was recommended.
- At the next review, the team will compare family logs, classroom examples, and direct observations. The family may request an earlier meeting if priorities, health, or daily routines change.

NC Infant-Toddler Program IFSP Review — Fictional Training Record

Review date: October 5, 2026. Child: Emilia Torres, called Emi at home. Date of birth: August 5, 2024; current age: 26 months. Record number: ITP-4827061; Medicaid member number: 684209731Q; service authorization: SLP-260105-47. This review updates the initial IFSP dated April 6, 2026. The family participated in Spanish and English. The bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist wrote this narrative from caregiver interviews, direct observation, and records available with family consent. The family received a Spanish explanation of each outcome and selected the routines where support would be most useful.

### Información de la familia

The household includes mamá Lucía Torres, papá Daniel Vega, and sister Luz Vega, age 6 years. Abuela Rosa Vega provides afternoon care. The family lives at 418 Marigold Lane, Cedarloma, North Carolina 27987, in Paloma County. The preferred telephone number is (919) 555-0142, and the family email is lucia.torres@example.com. Spanish is the primary home language; English is common during daycare routines. The family wants both languages supported. Their dog, Rocky, often joins floor play and provides a familiar reason to communicate.

Service coordinator Elena Paredes works through Paloma County CDSA, located at 72 Lantern Court, Cedarloma, North Carolina 27987. Her telephone number is (919) 555-0168, and her email is elena.paredes@example.com. Bilingual SLP Nora Salcedo provides services through Carolina Lantern Pediatric Communication. The clinician can be reached at (984) 555-0116 or nora.salcedo@example.com. The family information page lists https://carolinalantern.example.com/familias. Caregivers prefer telephone calls in Spanish and brief written summaries in both languages. They asked that appointment changes reach both parents.

The birth history identifies delivery at 34 weeks 2 days gestation, birth weight 2,140 g, and Apgar scores of 7 and 9 at one and five minutes. Emilia received neonatal care in the NICU at Marshglass Health–Riverbend Campus. The discharge summary describes feeding support and observation before discharge on August 24, 2024. Pediatrician Dr. Anika Rivas follows the child at Marshglass Health Pediatrics–Cedar Campus. The family reports no current feeding equipment, oxygen, or daily medication. Caregivers will bring any new medical recommendations to the next team contact.

At Marshglass Health ENT and Audiology–Riverbend Campus, audiologist Owen Mercado completed a hearing visit on September 18, 2026. The available report describes responses adequate for access to conversational speech during that visit. ENT physician Dr. Mara Ibarra recommended follow-up if caregivers notice changes in hearing or repeated ear symptoms. The coordinator reviewed this report with the family. No new hearing concern emerged during this review. The SLP will continue asking about responses to quiet speech during familiar routines and will share concerns with the medical team after obtaining the family's consent.

Mamá Lucía Torres said, “Yo sé lo que quiere muchas veces, pero cuando no entiendo, se tira al piso. Quiero que pueda pedir ayuda sin llorar.” Papá Daniel Vega added, “At dinner I want a little conversation, aunque sea con gestos y una palabra. No queremos quitarle el español.” Their first priority is easier communication during meals and transitions. Their second priority is participation with other children. They also want caregivers to recognize communication attempts consistently, especially when a word sounds different from the adult model.

Abuela Rosa Vega said, “Cuando estamos solas, me trae los zapatos y yo entiendo. En otros lugares, nadie sabe qué está diciendo.” Sister Luz enjoys pretend cooking and sometimes answers for the child. The family agreed that adults will pause before interpreting every gesture. They will also show the sibling how to offer choices without testing or correcting. Caregivers described strengths in shared laughter, imitation of actions, interest in songs, and persistence when finding a favorite toy. They want the plan to build on these strengths.

### Rutinas diarias y apoyos

Breakfast begins around 7:15 a.m., followed by dressing and departure around 8:00 a.m.. Emilia points toward foods, brings an empty cup, and sometimes says “más” or “agua”. The family will keep two choices visible and wait before offering either one. During dressing, an adult will describe the next action in the language that feels natural. A gesture, picture selection, or spoken attempt will count as communication. The family asked that practice stay brief because mornings already include work preparation and transportation.

Emi attends Little Lantern Early Learning House in Ms. Lopez's room. Lead teacher Ms. Marisol Lopez and assistant teacher Tessa Kim describe stronger participation during songs than during cleanup. Classmates Noah Bell and Inés Mora often play beside the child at the kitchen center. Staff will place familiar objects within view, provide a short invitation, and allow time to respond. The classroom will use the same simple picture choices as home. Adults will avoid requiring a spoken word before allowing access to a needed item.

Afternoons include a snack, outdoor play, and time with abuela. Dinner starts around 6:15 p.m., and the bedtime routine begins around 7:45 p.m.. During observation, the child pointed toward the dog and said “Rocky run”. The name in that production refers to the family pet. Caregivers can expand the message naturally while following the child's attention. Bath play supports requests such as “abre” and “again”. The family prefers a small basket of routine materials that adults can move between rooms.

Other supports include Paloma County WIC, Paloma Family Smart Start, and Paloma County DSS. These agencies provide nutrition appointments, a playgroup connection, and assistance reviewing childcare resources. No duplicate speech service is currently listed. Mamá works for Cedar Lantern Textiles, and papá works for Riverbend Parcel Works. Their changing shifts affect appointment availability. Community playgroup volunteer Mina Corral helps arrange activities but does not provide clinical treatment. The coordinator will begin transition conversations concerning Meadow Lantern Primary School when the family is ready to discuss future options.

The bilingual evaluation on September 29, 2026 included PLS-5 Spanish, caregiver interview, play observation, and a language sample. Auditory Comprehension yielded standard score 78, 7th percentile, confidence interval 73-83, and age equivalent 1;8. Expressive Communication yielded standard score 74, 4th percentile, confidence interval 69-81, and age equivalent 1;5. Total Language yielded standard score 75 and 5th percentile. These results describe performance during this evaluation. The team also considered communication across languages, caregiver examples, and participation in daily routines when selecting supports.

Clinical documentation uses ICD-10 F80.2. The evaluation entry uses CPT 92523; individual treatment entries use CPT 92507 with modifier GN when applicable. During supported play, Emilia followed familiar directions in 8/10 opportunities, or 80%, with min cues. Independent requests occurred in 3 of 5 opportunities. The sample included “ma” for “más” and “awa” for “agua”. An emerging /k/ appeared during imitation; [w] occurred in a familiar English word. One expanded utterance received SALT code [EW]. These observations guide functional support, without making speech sound accuracy the family's main outcome.

### Resultados y estrategias

Outcome 1: By January 5, 2027, Emilia will communicate a choice, request, or need during meals and play in 4 of 5 opportunities across home and daycare routines. Baseline performance is 3 of 5 with adult support. Adults will offer two meaningful choices, pause, and respond to gestures or words. The SLP will coach caregivers using Enhanced Milieu Teaching and Focused Stimulation. Models may include “más”, “help”, and “otro”. The family will note successful moments on a simple weekly sheet, sin convertir la comida en examen.

Outcome 2: By January 5, 2027, Emi will participate in cleanup and departure by understanding a familiar direction and communicating readiness or a need for support in 8/10 opportunities. Current performance varies by routine and available adult support. Caregivers and teachers will preview the change, show a picture, and use one short direction. They will model “all done”, “vamos”, or “ayuda” without demanding repetition. The SLP will reduce assistance from mod cues toward min cues as participation improves. Adults will record distress separately from communication success.

Outcome 3: By January 5, 2027, Emilia will exchange actions, gestures, or words with a sibling or classmate for three reciprocal turns in 4 of 5 supported play opportunities. Baseline observation showed two reciprocal turns with adult help. Sister Luz and classmates Noah and Inés can join familiar pretend cooking or rolling games. Adults will comment, wait, and help each child notice the other's message. Caregiver coaching will draw on Hanen interaction strategies. Participation will count in either language. Sharing a message matters more than matching the adult's exact wording.

Outcome 4: By January 5, 2027, participating caregivers will demonstrate three agreed communication strategies during two daily routines with 80% consistency across observed opportunities. These strategies are waiting, offering meaningful choices, and expanding the child's message. Initial observation showed 40% consistency. The clinician will demonstrate one strategy, invite practice, and ask what felt useful. Caregivers may decline a suggested activity and choose another routine. The team will use brief reflection: “¿Qué funcionó hoy?” Written examples will include Spanish and English. Progress will reflect caregiver confidence and workable routines alongside the recorded data.

Services will begin under this updated plan on October 12, 2026 and continue through January 5, 2027, subject to the next review. The schedule below reflects the family's selected times.

| Service and frequency | Day | Start | Stop | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Individual speech-language intervention, weekly | Tuesday | 9:00 a.m. | 9:45 a.m. | Little Lantern Early Learning House, Ms. Lopez's room |
| Caregiver coaching, twice monthly | Thursday | 4:15 p.m. | 5:00 p.m. | 418 Marigold Lane, Cedarloma |
| Service coordination, monthly | Friday | 12:00 p.m. | 12:30 p.m. | Paloma County CDSA, telephone participation |

The SLP will confirm attendance before travel and document the routine, caregiver participation, communication opportunities, and response to support after each visit. A missed visit will prompt contact about another available time. The family can request changes when work shifts or childcare arrangements change. Home coaching will include whichever caregiver is present and willing to participate. Daycare sessions will occur within familiar activities when practical. The coordinator will check whether the schedule remains useful at the monthly contact. Transportation needs, illness, and family events will be discussed without treating attendance as a measure of caregiver effort.

At the review, both parents agreed that the outcomes reflect their priorities and that Spanish should remain central to family interaction. The team explained consent, record sharing, and the process for requesting another meeting. The family approved sharing routine strategies with daycare staff and the listed providers. The next IFSP review is scheduled for January 5, 2027. The clinician will bring updated observations, caregiver examples, and service attendance information. Prepared by Nora Salcedo, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist, on October 5, 2026. Service coordinator Elena Paredes will provide the completed copies to the family.

IFSP REVIEW — NC INFANT-TODDLER SERVICES

- This fictional training document describes an individualized family service plan review. All people, organizations, locations, contacts, and records are invented.
- Review date: October 14, 2026. Initial IFSP date: July 16, 2026. Next review: January 14, 2027.
- Child: Emilio Rafael Solano. Preferred name: Milo. Birth date: August 14, 2024. Current age: 26 months.
- Meeting format: home visit with telephone participation from classroom staff. The family chose English and Spanish throughout discussion, documentation, and coaching.

INFORMACIÓN DE LA FAMILIA

- Mother: Marisol Vega Solano. Father: Andrés Solano Cruz. Both parents share caregiving decisions and request copies of this plan.
- Home address: 418 Willowglass Lane, Briarhaven, North Carolina 27963, in Brindle County. The family prefers visits in the living room.
- Older sister: Inés Solano, age 6 years. She enjoys singing with her brother and sometimes answers before he can respond.
- Maternal grandmother: Teresa Vega. Cousins Paloma Vega and Nico Vega visit during weekend meals. Babysitter Elena Ríos covers occasional evening shifts.
- Mother works at Juniper Kite Packing Cooperative. Father works at Copper Acorn Bicycle Works. Their changing schedules affect who attends sessions.

CONTACTOS Y COORDINACIÓN

- Service coordinator: Naomi Bell Treviño, assigned through Brindle County CDSA Office. Telephone: 919-555-0146. Email: naomi.trevino@example.invalid.
- Bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist: Julia Ortiz Mendoza, also identified in scheduling notes as J. Ortiz. Employer: Riverglass Pediatric Communication, PLLC.
- Clinician telephone: 984-555-0128. Clinician email: j.ortiz@example.invalid. Fictional service information page: https://riverglass.example.invalid/infant-services.
- Primary family telephone: 252-555-0164. Secondary telephone: 252-555-0181. Family email: solano.family@example.invalid. Text messages may address scheduling only.
- CDSA child record: BC-ITP-260814-073. Medicaid member number: 684207193Q. Speech service authorization: SLP-261019-4482.

HISTORIA Y PARTICIPACIÓN

- Family reports birth at Willowglass Women and Children’s Hospital, with gestational age 39 weeks, 2 days and birth weight 3.21 kg.
- Reported Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. These details come from a fictional intake summary.
- Pediatrician Dr. Avery Chen at Briarhaven Children’s Medical Center follows growth and routine health needs. No new family concerns about feeding safety were reported.
- Audiologist Priya Nolen completed a hearing visit on September 9, 2026. The supplied fictional report documented responses adequate for the assessment activities.
- Eligibility remains documented under ICD-10 F80.2. Intervention addresses functional communication across both languages and the routines the family selected.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES — EN SUS PALABRAS

- Mother said, “Quiero entender lo que necesita antes de que llore. Sometimes I guess, pero no siempre adivino bien.”
- Father said, “At dinner he brings my hand to the refrigerator. Quiero que pueda pedir ayuda sin frustrarse tanto.”
- Grandmother said, “Él entiende nuestras canciones. Necesitamos saber cómo darle tiempo para contestar, sin hablar por él.”
- The parents prioritize asking for food, requesting help, joining familiar play, and understanding simple directions. They want useful communication, aunque todavía no sea una frase completa.
- Mother added, “Please keep Spanish in the plan. Es el idioma de nuestra casa, y no queremos perderlo.”
- The family prefers strategies that fit ordinary routines. They requested short practice opportunities and shared examples that caregivers can use without buying materials.

RUTINAS DIARIAS — ASÍ ES NUESTRO DÍA

- Wake-up usually begins at 6:45 a.m.. Dressing works best when an adult offers two items and waits. Rushing increases pulling, crying, and leaving the activity.
- Breakfast occurs around 7:20 a.m.. Familiar foods create communication opportunities. The family will place choices within view and accept pointing, gestures, or words.
- Arrival at the classroom is near 8:10 a.m.. A picture sequence supports the transition from the doorway to putting belongings away and choosing play.
- Pickup is usually at 4:35 p.m.. Adults will share one successful communication example. Long explanations during pickup are difficult because several families arrive together.
- Dinner begins around 6:15 p.m.. Bath follows at 7:05 p.m., with bedtime reading near 7:40 p.m.. These routines offer predictable turns.

ENTORNO EDUCATIVO Y PERSONAS PRESENTES

- Emilio attends The Lantern-Pear Orchard, located at 62 Moonbasket Court, Briarhaven. The unusual program name refers to its pretend garden classroom.
- Lead teacher Ms. Celia Morrow and assistant Mr. Benito Hale agreed to use the same waiting and choice strategies during snack and play.
- Classmates Tavi Brooks and Luma Reed often play nearby. Adults will support brief exchanges while respecting each child’s interest and space.
- The family dog, Pipoca, often joins floor play. Neighbor M.R. sometimes greets the family outside but has no service responsibilities.
- Cousin Nico Vega enjoys rolling cars together. Babysitter Elena Ríos requested examples in Spanish because she usually provides care in that language.

EVALUACIÓN Y OBSERVACIONES CLÍNICAS

- Assessment date: September 24, 2026, at age 25 months. Sources included caregiver interview, play observation, language sampling, and selected standardized assessment activities.
- PLS-5 results in the fictional report included Auditory Comprehension standard score 78, percentile 7, and confidence interval 73-85.
- Expressive Communication standard score was 75, percentile 5, with confidence interval 70-83. Total Language standard score was 75, percentile 5.
- Reported age-equivalent ranges were 1;6–1;9 for receptive items and 1;3–1;6 for expressive items. These estimates do not define the child’s overall developmental age.
- English test results were considered alongside Spanish observations. Scores alone did not represent communication across both languages, cultural experience, or everyday participation.
- Observed strengths included shared enjoyment, imitation of actions, familiar song anticipation, and repair through gestures. Spontaneous productions included "agua", "más", and "go".
- One spontaneous production was “Pipoca ven.” The language sample included [EW] where an extra word occurred. Speech examples included [w] and emerging /m/.

OTRAS AGENCIAS Y APOYOS

- Brindle County WIC supports nutrition appointments and food access. The family will contact that office directly about appointment changes and approved food substitutions.
- Brindle County DSS provides benefit coordination. Case contact Ms. Dalia Finch may receive scheduling information only within the family’s written release.
- Brindle County Smart Start Partnership for Children supplied a fictional lending-library referral. The parents requested board books and simple picture materials for home routines.
- Brindle County Early Head Start is reviewing an application. Family contact Owen Mercado will explain availability; enrollment is pending and is not an IFSP service commitment.
- Naomi Bell Treviño will coordinate approved communication among agencies. Each release must identify the recipient, purpose, information, and expiration date before records are shared.

OUTCOME 1 — PEDIR DURANTE LAS COMIDAS

- Family outcome: During meals, Milo will communicate a choice or request so adults can respond with less guessing and the meal can continue comfortably.
- Criteria: Use a gesture, picture, sign, or spoken word in 4 of 5 opportunities across three meals, with min cues, documented by caregiver notes.
- Strategies: Offer two visible choices, pause, follow the child’s attention, and model "agua", "más", or "more". Accept either language without requiring repetition.
- Adults will respond promptly to meaningful attempts. They will avoid holding needed food beyond a brief opportunity and will stop practice when frustration increases.
- Baseline: Requests occurred in 2 of 5 opportunities with mod cues. Review evidence will include home examples and a snack observation.

OUTCOME 2 — PEDIR AYUDA

- Family outcome: During play and dressing, Emilio will ask for assistance before leaving the activity or pulling an adult toward the problem.
- Criteria: Communicate help in 3 of 5 naturally occurring opportunities across two routines, with min cues, for two consecutive weeks.
- Strategies: Model "help", "ayuda", or "abre". Pair words with an open-hand gesture. Provide help immediately after a clear attempt.
- Begin with familiar containers and clothing tasks. Adults may provide mod cues initially, then reduce support as the child anticipates the exchange.
- Baseline: Help requests occurred in 1 of 5 opportunities with max cues. The family will record one example when an opportunity occurs.

OUTCOME 3 — JUGAR CON OTROS

- Family outcome: During classroom and family play, Milo will join a short shared activity with another child while communicating a turn, choice, or protest.
- Criteria: Participate in three reciprocal turns in 4 of 5 observed play episodes, with mod cues, across home and classroom settings.
- Strategies: Use rolling cars, bubbles, songs, and turn-taking games. Model "mi turno", "your turn", and "stop", while honoring gestures and refusal.
- Sister Inés Solano can model one turn and wait. Classmate Luma Reed may participate when interested; adults will not assign another child a treatment role.
- Baseline: Two reciprocal turns occurred in 2 of 5 episodes. Adults will count successful exchanges rather than time spent sitting beside another child.

OUTCOME 4 — COMPRENDER EN LAS RUTINAS

- Family outcome: During familiar transitions, Emilio will understand a simple direction well enough to participate with less repeated adult prompting.
- Criteria: Follow familiar directions in 8/10 opportunities, with min cues, across two routines. Adults may present the direction in either language.
- Strategies: Pair one short direction with the relevant object or picture. Model "shoes on", "pon zapatos", or "give me", then wait.
- Baseline was 40% with mod cues. Adults will reduce verbal repetition and track whether the picture, gesture, or spoken direction supported participation.

SERVICIOS, FECHAS Y LUGARES

- Speech-language intervention: one 45-minute session weekly, from October 19, 2026 through January 18, 2027. Visits will alternate between home and classroom according to family priorities.
- Responsible clinician: Julia Ortiz Mendoza. Sessions include direct interaction and caregiver coaching. Fictional billing reference: CPT 92507, with modifier GN when applicable.
- Service coordination: one planned monthly contact plus contacts needed for referrals, scheduling, and review preparation, from October 14, 2026 through January 14, 2027.
- Classroom consultation: one 20-minute discussion monthly with Ms. Celia Morrow, included within the speech service arrangement. No separate therapy session is assigned to classmates.
- Missed visits will be rescheduled when feasible. The coordinator will document the reason, family preference, and new date. Changes require an updated service agreement.

ESTRATEGIAS COMPARTIDAS — PRÁCTICA EN CASA

- Coaching uses Hanen-informed interaction strategies, including following the child’s lead and waiting. The family is not enrolled in a separate branded course.
- Picture supports may borrow simple principles from PECS, but this plan does not document delivery of the complete protocol. Pictures supplement gestures and spoken language.
- Caregivers will practice during one chosen routine each day. No worksheets are required. Spanish remains available throughout play, meals, dressing, and comfort.
- The clinician will demonstrate, invite caregiver practice, and ask what worked. Cada intento cuenta; the adult responds to meaning before considering sound accuracy.
- No speech sound drill is assigned for /k/ or /ɾ/. Functional communication and participation remain the priorities described in this review.

SEGUIMIENTO, DERECHOS Y TRANSICIÓN

- The family may accept, decline, or request changes to individual services. The coordinator explained consent, record access, complaint options, and communication in the preferred language.
- Progress review will compare routine examples with each outcome’s criteria. Counts describe opportunities observed and will not be presented as general ability across all settings.
- A transition discussion is planned for May 14, 2027, when the child will be 33 months. Possible preschool supports will be discussed without assuming eligibility.
- The coordinator will confirm timelines, obtain any required releases, and arrange discussion with the appropriate education contact. The family requested continued Spanish access during transition planning.
- Parents agreed that the written priorities reflect their concerns. Mother said, “Sí, esto se parece a nuestra vida.” Father requested that strategies remain practical during workdays.

ACUERDOS Y RESPONSABILIDADES

- Marisol Vega Solano will share meal examples. Andrés Solano Cruz will share play examples. Either parent may revise the selected routine.
- J. Ortiz will bring picture choices and demonstrate strategies at the first visit. Naomi Bell Treviño will confirm scheduling and current releases.
- Electronic acknowledgment date: October 14, 2026. Family participation, provider responsibilities, and service dates are documented for this fictional IFSP review.
